| Area | Score | Note |
|---|---|---|
| DRY / consistency | 90 | 1 finding (P3) |

## Worth a ticket

**1. The fix is applied in 1 of 3 places** · P3 · DRY/consistency · validator CONFIRMED (95), refuter STANDS
- **Where:** `src/modules/spaces/domain/space-safes.repository.ts:48`, with the same pattern unchanged at `src/modules/spaces/domain/address-books/address-book-items.repository.ts:184` and `src/modules/spaces/domain/address-books/user-address-book-items.repository.ts:158`
- **What:** Both address-book repositories still build `` `...You can only add up to ${max - existing} more.` `` with no guard. When a space or user is already at the limit, users still see "You can only add up to 0 more." If they are over the limit, the number goes negative.
- **Proof:** `src/modules/spaces/routes/address-books.controller.e2e-spec.ts:522` asserts the "…up to 0 more." text today. No shared message helper exists.
- **Fix:** Apply the same `remaining > 0` ternary in both repositories and update the e2e expectation at L522. Otherwise, pull the message into one small shared helper. Out of scope for this commit ("…max amount of safes") is fine, but it's worth tracking.

**2. The negative-remaining branch has no test** · P3 · Testing · I checked this one myself; it didn't go to the agent pair
- **Where:** `src/modules/spaces/domain/space-safes.repository.integration.spec.ts:435`
- **What:** The new test covers `remaining === 0`, and reverting the change does make it fail, because Jest's `toThrow(new BadRequestException(msg))` requires an exact message match. Nothing covers `existing > max`, which is the case where the old code said "add up to -N more". The `> 0` guard also handles it, but no test protects it.
- **Fix:** Optionally, seed `maxSafesPerSpace + 1` rows directly through the database repo, or make the config mock return a smaller limit, then assert the short message.

## Not sure about / Ruled out / Not checked
- **Pre-existing, not part of this change:** the limit check at `space-safes.repository.ts:46-54` reads the count and inserts separately, not atomically. Two concurrent requests could both pass it and exceed the limit. It's unchanged by this diff, so it isn't scored.
- **Ruled out:** nothing.
- **Not checked:** I didn't run `yarn format`, `lint` or `test`, as you asked.

## Worth tidying
The only candidate is the shared limit-message helper from finding 1, and that finding already covers it. I have no other proposals.

## How this was produced
I ran the scope, profile and all nine category passes myself. The two subagents I was allowed were one validator and one refuter, both on finding 1. I modified no files and posted nothing.
